memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: A river watering the garden flowed from Eden; from there it was separated into four headwaters. The name of the first is the Pishon; it winds through the entire land of Havilah, where there is gold... The name of the second river is the Gihon... The name of the third river is the Tigris... And the fourth river is the Euphrates. — Gen 2:10–14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At first glance, this passage reads almost like a map. It names a river flowing out of Eden that divides into four—the Pishon, the Gihon, the Tigris, and the Euphrates—and mentions the lands they reach and the gold found there. These are real places and real details, grounding the garden in actual geography. The Bible is not telling us a fairy tale; it is recording something that truly happened.

But pause and notice the picture it paints. One river flows out from Eden and becomes four, spreading water far and wide, carrying life to distant lands. Eden was not a sealed, private paradise. God's provision overflowed its borders. Where God dwells, life flows outward.

We should not turn each river into a hidden symbol—Scripture does not ask us to. Yet the pattern of God's overflowing goodness runs right through the Bible. His blessing is never meant to stop with us; it flows through us to others.

This points forward beautifully. Jesus promised that whoever believes in Him would have rivers of living water flowing from within them (John 7:38–39). And Scripture ends with a river of the water of life flowing from God's throne (Rev 22:1). The God whose abundance watered Eden still pours out life today—in Christ, and through His people. Let His goodness flow through you to a thirsty world.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you see God's blessings as things to keep, or as gifts to let flow to others?
- In what way might God want His life to flow through you this week?
- How does Jesus' promise of "living water" speak to your own thirst?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord God, thank You that Your goodness overflows and brings life. Fill me with Your living water through Jesus, and let it flow out of me to bless the people around me. Amen.
